findings.observed: The second put raises OverflowError, but 'b' remains appended; len(q) is 2 and subsequent gets return 'a' then 'b'.
findings.expected: The second put raises OverflowError without changing the queue; len(q) remains 1 and only 'a' is queued.
findings.explanation: put appends before checking capacity and does not undo the append when the capacity check fails, violating the promised no-change behavior for a full put.

findings.trigger: a = TaskQueue(2); b = TaskQueue(2); a.put('x'); b.get()
findings.observed: b.get() returns 'x' even though no item was put into b.
findings.expected: b remains empty and b.get() raises IndexError because separate TaskQueue instances are independent.
findings.explanation: The mutable default items list is created once and reused by every instance constructed without an explicit items argument, so those instances share queue storage.
